evals.name: called-for-one-tracker-ticket-every-message-opens-with-the-frame-line
evals.prompt: work the decision map docs/decision-map/ado-193-ips-api-feed/ for #196, stage plan (2/4). Rows of #196: AC-1 "Initial full seed populates all active and pre-appointment IPS cases", AC-2 "Daily delta sync updates modified cases idempotently by mgw_casecode", AC-3 "Every synced case record includes resolved emails and the appointment status", AC-4 "Transient network or API errors are logged with structured retry handling". The map is local. Its open tickets and the Touches sentence of each Question: 196-match-key (grilling) 'Touches #144, #196 AC-2.'; 196-retry-shape (grilling) 'Touches #196 AC-4.'; 196-staff-source (task) 'Touches #196.'; 195-ip-loss-recovery (task) 'Touches #195 AC-1 and #196.'; 197-counts-and-owner (task) 'Touches #197 AC.'. Milestones, in map order: sync-ready [196-match-key, 196-retry-shape, 196-staff-source], decide-now [195-ip-loss-recovery], timesheet-ready [197-counts-and-owner]. 196-retry-shape is blocked by 196-match-key; nothing is claimed. I ask which one you recommend, then accept it ("yes, that one"); the ticket you recommend has two questions. After both answers, close it.
evals.expected_output: Every message to the person opens with the Frame line. The frontier lists the tickets for #196 first under a heading with their count, then one line for the rest of the map, and recommends inside the #196 group. Each grilling question opens '#144, #196 AC-2 · 196-match-key · question N of 2 · plan (2/4)'. The close report opens '#144, #196 AC-2 · 196-match-key closed · plan (2/4): #196 has 3 open'.
assertions: The first line of the frontier message is '#196 · map ado-193-ips-api-feed · plan (2/4)' and nothing comes before it

The frontier shows a heading 'Tickets for #196' with the count '4 of 4 open' (196-match-key, 196-retry-shape, 196-staff-source and 195-ip-loss-recovery, which touches #196 too), each with its type and, when its Touches sentence names one, the AC line of #196 (195-ip-loss-recovery shows no AC line, because its sentence names #196 with no AC line)
After the group, one line says 'Other tickets on this map: 1 for #197' and names 197-counts-and-owner
The recommendation is 196-match-key, chosen inside the #196 group (the earliest incomplete milestone with a takeable ticket, then the ticket that unblocks the most), not 197-counts-and-owner
The first question opens with the line '#144, #196 AC-2 · 196-match-key · question 1 of 2 · plan (2/4)' before any context or question text
The second question opens with '#144, #196 AC-2 · 196-match-key · question 2 of 2 · plan (2/4)'
The close report opens with '#144, #196 AC-2 · 196-match-key closed · plan (2/4): #196 has 3 open'
No message to the person in the run opens with a heading, a table or prose before the Frame line
The Touches sentence of the ticket is read from the ticket file, not from read or frontier output
After the Other line, no milestone-grouped list follows; the destination line and decisions so far come between the Frame line and the group

evals.name: a-direct-call-still-opens-every-question-with-the-frame-line
evals.prompt: continue the map docs/decision-map/ado-193-ips-api-feed/ (local). No tracker ticket was named. Open tickets: 196-retry-shape (grilling) whose Question ends 'Touches #196 AC-4.'; 197-counts-and-owner (task) whose Question ends 'Touches #197 AC.'. Milestones: sync-ready [196-retry-shape], timesheet-ready [197-counts-and-owner]. I pick 196-retry-shape. It needs one question; I do not know how many more.
evals.expected_output: The frontier is shown by milestone as before (no tracker group, because none was named). The question opens '#196 AC-4 · 196-retry-shape · question 1 · work-map'.
assertions: The frontier is grouped by milestone and has no 'Tickets for #' heading
The first question opens with '#196 AC-4 · 196-retry-shape · question 1 · work-map' - the tracker part comes from the ticket's Touches sentence, there is no 'of M' and the stage part is 'work-map'
The frontier message's first line is 'map ado-193-ips-api-feed · work-map'
